chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abdullah from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Fadhal said:
Muhammad ibn 'Ali asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), saying to him: 'I ran one lap (shawt), then the dawn rose.' He said to him: 'Pray, then return and complete your running (sa'y).'

key_terms.سَعْي: Sa'y: The ritual walking between the hills of Safa and Marwa during Hajj or Umrah.
key_terms.شَوْط: Shawt: A single lap or circuit between Safa and Marwa.
key_terms.صَلِّ: Salli: An imperative command to perform the prayer.
key_terms.طَلَعَ الْفَجْر: Tala'a al-fajr: The rising of the dawn, marking the beginning of the Fajr prayer time.

ai.seo_question: What should a pilgrim do if Fajr time enters while performing Sa'y?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this narration from Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies the procedural flexibility of Sa'y, demonstrating that the ritual is not invalidated by a necessary interruption for obligatory prayer. It highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle that the continuity of the ritual act is preserved even when paused for a higher obligation, ensuring the pilgrim’s effort remains valid upon resumption.
